national.line: A 10-year-old Jack Russell terrier named Luna is back home with her owners after surviving more than a month on her own in Yellowstone National Park after slipping out of a locked cabin on September 10.
A Harvard study that followed shy babies for years found shyness is inborn brain wiring, but most kids outgrow it: of 10 very shy one-year-olds, only 3 stay very shy as teenagers.
Florida first responders pulled a dog out of a sinkhole and got the pup safely reunited with its family.
Christian McCaffrey and his younger brother faced each other in an NFL game for the first time ever, then swapped jerseys afterward in a sweet brotherly moment.
Knicks forward Josh Hart showed up to the season opener with the NBA championship trophy braided right into his hair, and the video went viral.
Long drive champion Kyle Berkshire just smashed his own world record for the longest drive in golf, so the only person he had to beat was himself.
Elderly cats that were headed to be put down are getting a second chance at a retirement village built just for senior cats.
A California woman says she actually prefers sleeping on airport floors over hotel beds, and she even plans her trips around it, according to her viral video.
A cat who stayed kitten-sized his entire life surprised everyone, including his owners, by living all the way to the ripe old age of 14.
Dolly Parton is among the most searched Halloween costumes in the country this year, with fans hunting for ways to recreate four of her most iconic looks.

pride.label: All-District Tennis
pride.line: Congrats to Lebanon's Lilly Bradbury, who took fourth in singles, and Ava Johnson and Carli Alford, who took fourth in doubles, earning All-District honors in girls tennis. Coach Ron Crowell says the team plays district against Marshfield next.

pride.label: New Head Coach
pride.line: Congrats to Lebanon's Brittany Stamm, named the new head girls basketball coach for Lebanon R-3 Schools.

pride.label: New Head Coach
pride.line: Congrats to Lebanon's Kalem Copling, named the new head boys basketball coach for Lebanon R-3 Schools.

pride.label: National Budget Award
pride.line: Congrats to Lebanon's R-3 School District for earning a national Meritorious Budget Award.

pride.label: Grand Opening
pride.line: Congrats to Lebanon's R-3 School District on the opening of the new Robert W. Plaster Center for Student Success.

pride.label: Marching Festival
pride.line: Congrats to Lebanon's High School Marching Yellowjackets, who placed at the Valhalla Marching Festival at Parkview High School in Springfield on October 3.

pride.label: World Food Champ Finalists
pride.line: Congrats to Waynesville's Molly McDermitt, Cycila Keeney and Samantha Etheridge for reaching the finals of the World Food Championships in Indianapolis on October 18. Their dish - Bacon Lover's Christmas.

pride.label: Project Teach Award
pride.line: Congrats to Waynesville's Kyleen Oxendine, an East Elementary teacher, for winning the first-quarter Project Teach Award on October 19 for her Take Home Reading Success Kits.

pride.label: Tiger Spirit Trophy
pride.line: Congrats to Waynesville's Sixth Grade Center for winning the traveling Tiger Spirit Trophy again with a first-place finish in the 2026 Homecoming Parade.

pride.label: Community Recognition
pride.line: Congrats to Waynesville's Domino's for earning the school district's Community Recognition Plaque for October, for its ongoing support of students.

pride.label: Perfect Bus Inspection
pride.line: Congrats to Waynesville's R-6 school bus mechanics and drivers: all 10 buses in a surprise Missouri State Highway Patrol inspection on October 20 passed, a perfect 100 percent.

pride.label: Record Test Scores
pride.line: Congrats to Bolivar's school district for its best state test results since testing began in 1998, with math proficiency at 56.3 percent, 12.5 points above the state average.

pride.label: Banking School Grads
pride.line: Congrats to Bolivar's Lathan Martin and Boone Shockley of Grand Missouri Bank for graduating from the Oklahoma Bankers Association Consumer Lending School in Oklahoma City.

pride.label: Perfect Inspection
pride.line: Congrats to Bolivar's Parkview Health Care Facility for passing its annual state inspection without a single deficiency.

pride.label: Marching Festival
pride.line: Congrats to Marshfield's High School marching band for taking fourth place at the Ozark Mountain Marching Festival in Reeds Spring.

pride.label: 100 Years in Business
pride.line: Congrats to Marshfield's Chevrolet dealership on 100 years of serving the community, celebrated with a two-day anniversary party.

pride.label: New City Administrator
pride.line: Congrats to Osage Beach's new city administrator Keith Klostermann, a 30-year educator, appointed by Mayor Richard Ross.

pride.label: Football Win
pride.line: Congrats to Camdenton's Lakers for beating Capital City in a back-and-forth game, won on a go-ahead touchdown run by Michael Maschino.

local.line: The City of Lebanon has a second new city logo proposal on the table, along with a fresh city slogan: Build your journey here.
A Lebanon church built a wheelchair ramp for neighbor Tiffany Walker, who lives with a rare condition called Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, to make her daily life easier.
Lebanon R-3 Schools says its Hive Depot is giving Lebanon students essential resources along with new learning opportunities.
The Joel E. Barber C-5 school district is considering building a high school add-on to its existing building, Superintendent Dr. Rachelle Jennings says.
BTC Bank surprised the City of Buffalo with a 50,000 dollar check that completes the funding for phase one of the Buffalo Community Center repairs.
A developer wants to build a 126-room Hyatt hotel, under the Unscripted by Hyatt name, in the Backwater Jacks cove at Lake of the Ozarks.
Two new Missouri State Highway Patrol troopers from the 126th recruit class have been assigned to Camden and Miller counties in Troop F.
A Lake of the Ozarks nonprofit is helping women rebuild their lives with a safe place to sleep, a working phone, transportation and someone in their corner.
The U.S. Census Bureau says Seymour keeps growing, with the city's estimated population now at 2,247.
A Seymour hunter bagged a black bear in Missouri's fall season, one of seven bears taken in Zone 1 as of Monday morning since the season opened Saturday.
The Polk County Museum hosted a group of homeschoolers for a hands-on lesson in Cherokee history and customs.

music.line: Morgan Wallen's Sand in My Boots festival is heading back to Gulf Shores, Alabama, in 2027 after a year away, mixing country heavyweights with artists from other genres.
Chris Stapleton now has a second song with one billion Spotify streams, You Should Probably Leave, joining elite company.

Zach Bryan, who just turned 30 and reportedly sold his song catalog for 350 million dollars, has released an eight-song EP called Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs to go with a book about his life.
Jordan Davis has a new radio single called Mess, and he told Billboard the melody locked him in right away.
The Birthplace of Country Music Museum is celebrating America's 250th anniversary with music, history and special events.

weird.line: A Texas racetrack unveiled a giant cowboy hat sculpture for its upcoming Formula One race, and Guinness confirmed it's the largest cowboy hat in the world.
A Rhode Island man grew the first pumpkin ever to top 3,000 pounds, making his gargantuan gourd the largest fruit ever recorded.
A Cheyenne couple, Amy and Andy Corbin, broke Wyoming's heaviest pumpkin record for the fourth year in a row with a 2,224-pound pumpkin.
A kangaroo was on the loose in Kansas, and it became one of the most-talked-about trending stories just across the state line.
An Idaho sheriff's deputy came to the rescue of a moose that got its head and body tangled up in a roll of wire fencing.
Park workers in Ohio found an escaped emu wandering down a mountain bike trail and shared photos and video of the unexpected trail rider.
An emu got loose in California and led police officers on a chase, making for one very unusual police pursuit.
A bear broke into a library in California, and security cameras caught the whole thing.
An Asian elephant named Samudra stomped a 500-pound pumpkin flat at the Oregon Zoo's 28th annual Squishing of the Squash.
Lemurs at the Oregon Zoo got Halloween jack-o-lanterns with grapes hidden at the bottom, and they enjoyed every bit of them.
The San Diego Zoo picked the perfect day to announce a baby two-toed sloth was born: International Sloth Day.
A Zero electric motorcycle went 271.2 miles on a single charge, beating the old Guinness world record by just over 78 miles.
David Rush's wife and kids have now joined him in the Guinness World Records book, so every member of the Rush family is officially a record breaker.
An orphan kitten a man raised as a pet in Bolivia turned out to be a brand-new wild cat species, the first new member of the cat family described in more than 100 years.
A tiny dog played the drums in a rock band costume called Angine de Pawtrine at the 36th annual Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade in New York City.
The Oatmeal cartoonist Matthew Inman built a giant evil raccoon named Grimothy in his brother's front yard for Halloween, based on a viral chubby Seattle raccoon.
A massive moose was caught on video near the New York and Connecticut border, and the video is making the rounds online.
An angler at Lake Cascade set a new catch-and-release state record for bullhead catfish.
Minnesota's Pumpkin King is back on top with his fifth national giant pumpkin win.
The 38th Anamosa Pumpkinfest in Iowa saw its biggest pumpkin ever, breaking the event's all-time record last Saturday.
Texas firefighters rushed to rescue one of several escaped horses after it got stuck in a drainage ditch next to a busy highway.
Bidders are flocking to Union County, Pennsylvania, for one of the largest pumpkin auctions in the whole country.
A bear was spotted on the front porch of a home in Blakely, giving the family a very unexpected visitor at the door.

humor.line: It's Back to the Future Day, the date Marty McFly and Doc Brown traveled to in Part Two, and when the real date finally arrived, the movies played in almost 2,000 theaters.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Babbling Day, for anyone who talks nonstop about nothing, and here's the best part: another name for a babbler is a blatherskite.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Hagfish Day, honoring an eel-like fish with no bones, no jaws and no scales that can ooze enough slime to fill a two-gallon bucket in minutes.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Garbanzo Bean Day, and it was started by a company that makes chickpea snacks, so yes, the beans got their own holiday from a snack brand.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's World Bolognese Ragu Day, and the word ragu comes from a French word meaning to revive the taste, which is exactly what spaghetti night does.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Pumpkin Cheesecake Day, and while cheesecake goes all the way back to ancient Greece, nobody knows who first thought to put pumpkin in it.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Apple Day, which started in London in 1990, and fans celebrate by tasting apples, juicing them and even singing songs and reciting poems about apples.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Eat a Pretzel Day, and legend says a monk invented the soft pretzel in 610, shaping the dough like kids' arms folded in prayer and handing them out as rewards.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Tavern-Style Pizza Day, honoring the Chicago tavern that renamed itself the Home Run Inn in 1947 after a baseball crashed through its front window.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Nut Day, and here's the nutty part: a lot of what we call nuts technically aren't nuts at all, they're dried seeds.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Knee Day, celebrating the largest joint in your body, the one that works like a hinge and complains every time you stand up.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Clean Up the Earth Day, and it lands exactly six months after Earth Day as a halftime check on how we're doing.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Wombat Day, which also goes by Hug a Wombie Day and Wombats of the World Unite Day.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Boston Cream Pie Day, and here's the twist: Boston cream pie isn't a pie at all, it's a cake, first made at Boston's Parker House Hotel in 1856.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Mole Day, and it has nothing to do with the animal: chemistry fans celebrate from 6:02 a.m. to 6:02 p.m. in honor of Avogadro's number.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Croc Day, honoring the shoe that started out as a boat shoe in Boulder, Colorado, and a gold Croc released for the day once sold out in hours.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Canning Day, and canning exists because Napoleon's government offered a 12,000 franc prize to anyone who could figure out how to keep food from spoiling.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's TV Talk Show Host Day, held on Johnny Carson's birthday, the King of Late Night who hosted The Tonight Show for 30 years.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Bologna Day, and one famous kind is Lebanon bologna, made since the late 1800s by the Pennsylvania Dutch in Lebanon, Pennsylvania, not our Lebanon.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Good and Plenty Day, honoring the oldest candy brand in America, first made in Philadelphia in 1893.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's World Tripe Day, promoted by a group called the Tripe Marketing Board, and it's based on a 1662 diary entry where a man raved about an excellent dish of tripe.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's 40-Hour Work Week Day, marking the 1938 law that created the 40-hour work week and set the very first minimum wage at 25 cents an hour.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Food Day, started back in 1975 to be the Earth Day of eating, and when it came back in 2011 more than 2,300 events were held across the country.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Sourest Day, created by a man in Ann Arbor, Michigan, to honor his old roommate on his birthday, and the roommate's last name was Sauer.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Mother-in-Law Day, and holidays for mothers-in-law go back to at least the 1920s, so call her, fellas, she's been waiting a hundred years.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Greasy Foods Day, and the official advice for celebrating is: when in doubt, just deep fry whatever you have.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's World Pasta Day, born at the first World Pasta Congress in Rome in 1995, where countries met for the sole purpose of getting everyone to eat more pasta.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's World Pizza Makers Day, and pizza got its start in Naples back when Naples was not even part of Italy, it was its own kingdom.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Mule Day, marking 1785, when the King of Spain sent two donkeys to America, and George Washington used them to breed the country's first mules.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Texas Chicken Fried Steak Day, and the man behind it got turned down by both the Texas Department of Agriculture and the Texas Beef Council before he found a lawmaker who'd help.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Horseless Carriage Day, based on a 1769 diary entry about a strange new machine that moved without horses, powered by someone turning a handle.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Pumpkin Day, and the word pumpkin comes from a Greek word meaning large melon.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Mincemeat Day, and here's the funny part: a lot of modern mincemeat recipes don't have any meat in them at all.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Navy Day, and October 27 was picked because it's Theodore Roosevelt's birthday.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Potato Day, and potatoes were first grown in South America as far back as 7,000 years ago, but didn't reach New Hampshire until 1719.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's National Parmigiano Reggiano Day, and every wheel of the real stuff ages at least 12 months, and sometimes as long as 40 months, before it's ready.
humor.label: National Day

humor.line: It's Cranky Co-Workers Day, the one day you're supposed to let your grumpy co-worker stay cranky instead of trying to cheer them up.
humor.label: National Day
